problem.text: Leakage power in SRAM arrays has become a critical design concern as technology scales to sub-10nm nodes

evidence.quote: As technology scales to sub-10nm nodes, leakage power in SRAM arrays has become a critical design concern.

method.text: A 6T SRAM cell using independent-gate FinFET transistors with dual-threshold voltage scheme and asymmetric fin heights

evidence.quote: we propose a 6T SRAM cell using independent-gate FinFET transistors that significantly reduces standby leakage power while maintaining acceptable noise margins
The cell uses minimum-sized transistors at the 7nm technology node with fin pitch of 24nm.
HSPICE simulations using BSIM-CMG models confirm the design feasibility.
The standby leakage power is 8.3 pW/cell at Vdd=0.6V and 25°C
The static noise margin is 185 mV at nominal conditions, exceeding the minimum requirement of 150 mV.
The read access time is 0.42 ns at Vdd=0.8V.
The write margin was measured at 320 mV, confirming reliable write operation.

findings.text: The proposed 6T FinFET SRAM achieves 8.3 pW/cell standby leakage at 0.6V, a 45% reduction over conventional designs

evidence.quote: The standby leakage power is 8.3 pW/cell at Vdd=0.6V and 25°C, which represents a 45% reduction compared to the baseline 6T design.

findings.text: Independent-gate biasing with -0.2V back-gate voltage exponentially reduces subthreshold leakage

evidence.quote: By applying a negative back-gate voltage of -0.2V during standby mode, the subthreshold leakage is exponentially reduced.

findings.text: Static noise margin of 185 mV exceeds the 150 mV minimum requirement, confirming read stability

evidence.quote: The static noise margin is 185 mV at nominal conditions, exceeding the minimum requirement of 150 mV.

limitations.text: Temperature sensitivity and process variation effects across wider operating range not investigated

evidence.quote: Future work will investigate the temperature sensitivity and process variation effects across a wider operating range.
